newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CSFB denies it quits dealing in Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: CSFB denies it quits dealing in Frankfurt.

text.p: Investment bank Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) firmly denied that it was planning to cease its Frankfurt-based trading in equities, bonds and currencies, as reported by German magazine Boerse Online.
A spokesman for CSFB, part of Switzerland's CS Holding financial group, said the only activity CSFB would cease in Frankfurt was that of market-making or taking own positions in currencies.
This activity would be transferred to CSFB's other trading centres in Zurich, London, New York and Singapore as part of the company's global reorganisation.
"We are not stopping trading foreign exchange out of Frankfurt and will still be dealing for clients," a CSFB spokesman said.
CSFB's activities in equity trading in Frankfurt would in fact be increased, but the spokesman said he did not know how many additional people would be hired.
CSFB's activities in fixed income in Frankfurt would also be maintained, the spokesman added.

Earlier today a summary of a report by Boerse Online to be published in Thursday's editions said CSFB would cease its equity, bond and currency activities in Frankfurt by end-March 1997 as part of its reorganisation.
